Before The Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Arun Dev Choudhury Order 12.09.2024

Though an affidavit has been filed by the State respondent contending that the land acquisition process was carried out in terms of the Act, 1894, the case of the petitioner is that they are entitled for compensation in terms of Act, 2013 more particularly on the ground that the award was passed in 2015 and therefore they are entitled for the benefit under Section 24 of the Act, 2013.
In the aforesaid backdrop, the fundamental issue in this writ petition is whether the petitioner can be granted compensation in terms of the provision of Act, 1894 or they are entitled for better compensation under the provision of Act, 2013.
The principle in this regard has already been settled by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Indore Development Authority vs Manoharlal reported in 2020 SCC Online SC 316.

sentences.text: Therefore, to come into a conclusion, certain vital aspect of the matter should be brought on record by the State respondent, more particularly, the date and copy of the notification purportedly issued under Section 4 and Page No.# 3/3 Section 6 of the Act, 1894, the award that has been purportedly passed in the land acquisition process in question and any approval that has been sought or granted by the competent authority in terms of Section 11 of the Act, 1894 and the date taking over possession.
On the next date fixed, the aforesaid material be produced before this court either by way of instruction or by way of an affidavit.
In the meantime, the petitioner is permitted to file reply affidavit to the affidavit-in-opposition filed by the State.
List this matter in the 1st week of November, 2024.
